app.name: harness-switch
app.devMode: Local development mode: this page is served by a local dev server

login.title: Server configuration control plane
login.intro: Activating a profile writes directly to each CLI's own configuration files, with no shell setup required.
login.hint: Enter the web password printed in the terminal on first launch.

harness.subtitle: Manage profiles and safely write this tool's native configuration files.
harness.overwriteWarning: The profile overwrites the target files directly. A backup is taken first; verify connectivity and model availability after switching.
harness.deleteBlocked: Activate another profile before deleting this one
harness.deleteAdditiveExtra: Its provider entry in the configuration file is removed as well.
harness.officialHintClaude: Use Claude Code's own Anthropic account login
harness.officialHintCodex: Use Codex's own ChatGPT / OpenAI account login

profile.additiveNote: This tool's config file keeps providers side by side, so switching only moves the current pointer — the other providers you wrote by hand are left alone.
profile.providerNone: None (this profile carries its own key)
profile.vaultEmpty: The vault is empty. Add a provider entry under “Vault” at the top first.
profile.noEndpoints: This provider has no named endpoint, so the base URL below is used.
profile.name: Profile name
profile.renameHint: Renaming also updates the recorded active profile and the provider id in the native config.
profile.baseUrlFromVault: The base URL comes from vault endpoint “{{endpoint}}”.
profile.apiKeyKeep: Leave empty to keep the current key
profile.apiKeySharedHint: This profile references a shared provider; rotate the key in the vault instead.
profile.fallbackModelPlaceholder: Optional; used when no tier matches, e.g. glm-5
profile.claudeModelHint: Leave empty to keep Claude Code's default model; map the individual tiers below.
profile.saveFirst: Save this profile first, then reopen it to take over the raw file contents.
profile.rawIntro: Below is what is currently written to disk, generated from the fields as last saved. Editing any of them counts as taking it over by hand, and the form fields stop affecting that file.

mapping.title: Model mapping
mapping.intro: Display names only affect Claude Code's /model menu; an empty one shows the actual model ID. Turning on “1M context” appends [1m] to the model ID — only enable it for a model that really supports 1M.

error.nameSlash: A profile name cannot contain / or \
error.nameTooLong: A profile name is at most {{max}} characters
error.providerGone: The referenced provider no longer exists — pick another
error.endpointGone: The referenced endpoint no longer exists — pick another
error.checkFields: Check the fields marked in red.

vault.title: Vault
vault.intro: A provider entry keeps the API key in one place (AES-256-GCM encrypted, hidden by default) along with reusable endpoints. Profiles can reference an entry here instead of each holding its own copy of the key.
vault.formIntro: Set the credential and any reusable named endpoints; saving returns to the list.
vault.empty: The vault is empty — add a provider first.
vault.deleteBody: This deletes “{{name}}”. An entry referenced by a profile cannot be deleted — remove the reference first.
vault.name: Name
vault.apiKeyKeep: Leave empty to keep the current key
vault.endpointsHint: A profile referencing this provider can pick one of these endpoints, whose base URL then wins over the profile's own address.

error.endpointKeyInvalid: Cannot contain / or \, and is at most {{max}} characters
error.checkFields: Check the fields marked in red.

activate.title: Activate profile?
activate.body: This switches {{harness}} to "{{profile}}" and writes its native configuration files{{changed}}. Target local user: {{user}}. A backup is taken first.
activate.loadFailed: Could not read the content to be written: {{reason}}
activate.loading: Loading the content to be written…

env.title: Environment file compatibility
env.intro: Switching does not require it. Run this in the relevant shell only when Codex uses environment-variable authentication:
env.note: The file contains only variables recognized by each tool. Kimi Code and Pi do not read credentials from the shell, so their sections contain only a comment.

backup.restoreBody: This writes the {{harness}} / {{profile}} configuration files from {{time}} back to disk, overwriting the current content.
backup.written: Restored the files from that snapshot to disk.
backup.historyIntro: Every write snapshots the original files into the data directory, keeping the last 10. Only this tool’s history is listed; entries that match what is on disk are marked current.
backup.restoreHistoryBody: Red is what you lose, green is what the restore writes. Confirming overwrites the files on disk from this snapshot; the active profile harness-switch has on record does not roll back with it.

drift.title: Configuration drift
drift.legend: Red is what is on disk; green is what the active profile would write.
drift.noActiveProfile: This tool has no active profile.
drift.nothingToCompare: No active profile, so there is nothing to compare.
drift.allInSync: Every file matches the active profile.
drift.reapplyBody: This rewrites {{harness}}'s native configuration files from the active profile, overwriting local edits on disk. A backup is taken first.
drift.adoptBody: This writes the current on-disk content back into the profile, and later writes will use it as the source. This cannot be undone.
drift.reapplied: Rewrote {{harness}}'s native configuration files from the active profile.
drift.adopted: Adopted {{harness}}'s live configuration into the profile.

doctor.title: Diagnostics
doctor.intro: Checks tool installation, whether configuration files are readable, writable and parseable, storage permissions, and drift.

check.installMissing: No {{bin}} executable on PATH — the tool may not be installed
check.installNotRequired: {{harness}} is typically a web service — no PATH CLI is required
check.filePermissive: {{target}} is readable and writable, but its mode is {{mode}} — group/other can read it; 0600 is recommended
check.fileOk: {{target}} exists and is readable and writable ({{path}})
check.driftNoProfile: No active profile, so there is no drift to check
check.driftInvalid: The live files contain content that cannot be parsed
check.driftMismatch_one: {{count}} file does not match the active profile ({{status}})
check.driftMismatch_other: {{count}} files do not match the active profile ({{status}})
check.driftInSync: The live files match the active profile
check.probeNoProfile: No active profile; connectivity probe skipped
check.probeOfficialLogin: {{harness}} is on its built-in account login; no custom endpoint to probe
check.probeMissingCredential: Profile {{profile}} has no base URL or API key; cannot probe

notice.title: Written to disk
notice.activated: {{harness}} switched to "{{profile}}" (user: {{user}}); its native configuration files have been written.
notice.activatedHint: Claude Code picks this up immediately; Codex, Kimi Code and Pi need a restart.
notice.officialRestored: {{harness}} switched back to its official login (user: {{user}}); the third-party API route was removed from the native configuration.
notice.officialHint: If you have not logged in yet, start the tool in a terminal and complete its official login once.

operations.undone: Undid that operation on {{harness}}; both the native configuration files and the recorded active profile are back to where they were.
operations.title: Operation history
operations.intro: Every write to a native configuration file is recorded first, so after a power loss or a killed process the service rolls back whatever was left unfinished on its next start. Undo returns both the configuration files and the recorded active profile to their state before the operation.
operations.undoBody: This restores {{harness}}'s {{count}} native configuration files to their content before the operation and returns the recorded active profile with them. A snapshot is taken first.

profile.activeDeleteForbidden: This profile is in use; activate another one before deleting it

activation.officialLoginUnsupported: {{harness}} does not support official account login
activation.noActiveProfile: This tool has no active profile, so there is nothing to render
activation.officialProfileCannotAdopt: The official login is active, so there is no profile to adopt into
activation.adoptUnsupported: This tool cannot adopt a live configuration

provider.inUse_one: This credential is referenced by {{count}} profile; remove the reference first
provider.inUse_other: This credential is referenced by {{count}} profiles; remove the references first
provider.credentialUnreadable: Could not read the key for credential {{id}}

codex.loginCacheTooLarge: The Codex login cache file is too large and was skipped
codex.loginCacheInvalidJson: The Codex login cache is not valid JSON
codex.configDirectoryNotRegular: The Codex configuration directory is not a regular directory
codex.loginCacheNotRegular: The Codex login cache is not a regular file

sync.sourceCodexLoginCacheMissing: The source user has no usable Codex official login cache
sync.sourceEqualsTarget: The source and target users are the same

storage.corruptQuarantined: The data store is corrupt. The original was quarantined as {{quarantine}}; restore from a backup before continuing

probe.badUrl: Base URL does not parse, or is not http/https
probe.missingBaseUrl: No base URL supplied; nothing to test
probe.missingApiKey: No API key supplied; nothing to test
probe.networkError: Could not reach the endpoint (DNS, refused connection or TLS failure)
probe.unauthorized: Endpoint reachable but rejected the credential (HTTP {{status}}); check the API key
probe.invalidResponse: The response is not a recognized model-catalog format

activation.envRebuildFailed: The native configuration was written, but rebuilding env.sh failed
activation.officialEnvRebuildFailed: The official login was restored, but rebuilding env.sh failed
activation.backfillFailed: Could not save {{profile}}'s existing configuration back into the profile

provider.endpointFallback: Endpoint {{endpoint}} no longer exists; falling back to the provider's first endpoint

sync.activeReapplyFailed: The profile store was updated, but automatic re-activation failed: {{reason}}

transfer.activeRestoreFailed: Could not restore the active state: {{reason}}

sync.title: Sync from another user
sync.intro: Copies the source user's profiles and the credentials they reference to {{user}}. Active state, backups and native configuration files are not copied by default; migrating the Codex login cache is a separate opt-in.
sync.overwriteHint: Only checked harnesses are overwritten; unchecked ones keep the current user's version.
sync.migrateCache: Migrate the Codex official login cache (auth.json)
sync.migrateCacheHint: This copies a reusable Codex login session, not ordinary configuration. Choose it only when the target user is entitled to that login.
sync.migrateCacheOverwrite: The target user already has a login cache; continuing overwrites it and takes a backup first.
sync.storeOnlyHint: Syncing only writes to the profile store. Activate the profile you want after syncing to make it take effect.
sync.noOtherUsers: There are no other manageable local login users.
sync.confirmCacheBody: This copies {{source}}'s Codex official login cache (auth.json) to {{target}}. {{extra}}Continue only if the target user is entitled to use that login session.
sync.confirmCacheOverwrite: The target user already has a cache; it will be overwritten and backed up.
sync.confirmCacheFresh: The target user will get a new local login cache.
sync.confirmCacheAction: Migrate the login cache and sync
sync.done: Sync complete: {{imported}} added, {{overwritten}} overwritten, {{skipped}} skipped, {{providersCopied}} credentials copied.
sync.cacheMigrated: The Codex login cache was migrated.
sync.cacheNotMigrated: The Codex login cache was not migrated.

transfer.title: Move configuration
transfer.intro: Bring profiles and credentials onto this machine, or pack them up to take along. Every source writes to this manager’s own store.
transfer.exportIntro: The file is AES-256-GCM encrypted with the transfer passphrase, independent of this machine's local key.
transfer.passphraseMismatch: The two passphrases do not match.
transfer.exported: The encrypted export is ready. The passphrase is not written to the file — keep it separately.
transfer.importIntro: The file is decrypted and checked for conflicts first; nothing is written until you confirm. Profiles of the same name on this machine are kept by default.
transfer.pickFileHint: The file is decrypted by the server on this machine; nothing is sent to an external service.
transfer.notAnExport: Not a valid harness-switch export file
transfer.importPassphrasePlaceholder: The passphrase set at export time
transfer.previewStale: The import options changed — check the contents again before confirming.
transfer.policySkip: Keep this machine’s profile, skip the import
transfer.policyOverwrite: Overwrite this machine’s profile from the export
transfer.restoreActive: Restore the activation state from the export
transfer.confirmAuthTitle: Confirm a change to Codex auth.json?
transfer.confirmOverwrite_one: {{count}} of them has the same name and will be overwritten.
transfer.confirmOverwrite_other: {{count}} of them have the same name and will be overwritten.
transfer.confirmKeep: Profiles with the same name are kept, not overwritten.
transfer.cacheMigrated: the export's Codex login cache was migrated
transfer.cacheNotMigrated: the export's Codex login cache was not migrated

authEffect.openai-api-key: Restoring the selected Codex profile updates OPENAI_API_KEY in this machine's auth.json; that is not the same as migrating the export's full official login session.
authEffect.auth-override: Restoring the selected Codex profile writes that profile's raw auth override into this machine's auth.json.
authEffect.official-cleanup: Restoring Codex's official-login state may clear a leftover OPENAI_API_KEY from this machine's auth.json.

githubSync.title: GitHub Cloud Sync
githubSync.intro: Seamless multi-machine configuration synchronization using your GitHub account. Backups are end-to-end AES-256-GCM encrypted with a master passphrase before storing into a private Gist.
githubSync.deviceIntro: Enter the user code on GitHub to complete binding.
githubSync.tokenPlaceholder: Enter GitHub Token with gist permission (ghp_...)
githubSync.pushIntro: Encrypts all profiles and provider credentials on this machine and uploads to your private Gist.
githubSync.pushSuccess: Successfully synced to GitHub Gist ({{profiles}} profiles, {{vault}} credentials).
githubSync.pullIntro: Downloads the encrypted backup from your private Gist and decrypts it locally.
githubSync.codeExpired: The authorization code expired — request a new one.
githubSync.tokenScopeHint: The token needs the gist scope to read and write the encrypted config file.

import.title: Import existing configuration
import.intro: Reads what these five tools currently have on disk and picks out the providers that can be adopted. Neither the scan nor the import touches their configuration files; you have to activate a profile yourself before anything is written.
import.nameTaken: A profile with this name exists
import.keyOutsideConfig: credential is not in the config file
import.apiKeyFromEnv: This provider reads its credential from the environment, so it is not in the config file
import.overwriteExisting: Overwrite the existing profile with this name

note.unsupported: This tool does not support scan-and-import yet
note.noConfigFiles: No config file for this tool was found on disk
note.unparsable: The config file exists but cannot be parsed — fix it before importing
note.noCandidates: No importable provider was found in the config file
